## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Hive
where: HiveRepository (uses), src/persistence/repositories.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
private readonly items = new Map<string, Hive>();
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B

if (hive.ownerId !== ownerId) {
=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These are different concepts. A is the Hive itself: HiveRepository (node 22ea3eb4c082b330, src/persistence/repositories.ts) stores Hive entities in `private readonly items = new Map<string, Hive>();`. B is the Hive Owner, the person or beekeeper who owns a hive. TreatmentService (node 2912145e8ad12343, src/business/treatmentService.ts) only refers to the owner through the hive's ownerId attribute, in an authorization check: `if (hive.ownerId !== ownerId) {`. A hive refers to its owner, but the hive and its owner are separate real-world things, not one concept under two names.
